name: room
text: Room opened — goal: security: Paranoid guard: scan for leaks/injection; VERIFY elements are REAL (not fake/dead); DETECT

name: Warden
text:
**Decision:** We’ll run a **manual, human-led review** of every external link and embedded asset in the system before any automated scan. A person will click each one, watch for redirects, and check if the destination is real and safe.

**Why:** Automated tools can miss sneaky tricks—like a link that looks fine but secretly points to a phishing site. A human can spot odd behavior faster than a machine can be tricked. This is slower, but it’s the only way to be sure nothing slips through.

**Trade-off:** Speed. We’re choosing accuracy over automation, knowing it’ll take more time. But if we miss a leak, the cost is higher than a little extra effort now.

name: Audit
text: While a manual review seems thorough, it introduces significant risks related to human error and oversight. A better alternative could be combining an initial automated scan with a manual review of flagged items to efficiently identify potential threats while reducing the burden on individuals. To settle the argument, we could assess past incidents where manual reviews failed to catch security issues compared to the effectiveness of automated tools.
